page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Page number and running head at top. Heading "I. NOMEN." centred, followed by the first line of the next paragraph. Catchword at lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Accedo iam, optimi auditores, ad Pro-legomena, docendi gratia ἀμαθ[?] dicturus, primùm, de Nomine Habacuc Pro-phetæ: secundò, de eius Officio: tertiò, de Tempore quo is docuit & vaticinatus est: quartò, de genere Gaussæ, quod in hac Providentiæ, Iustitiæ & Misericordiæ Dei defensione dominatur: quintò, de Statu: postremò, de eius Confirmatione: deque totius istius libelli Oeconomia, quæ interrogatione & responsione constat.

De canonica vero Prophetiæ istius auctoritate, illud ὑπόληψιν[?] oportet, sacrosanctam & inuiolabilem semper fuisse & esse. Neque vero Habacuci συμφωνία solum cum Prophetis & Apostolis, in doctrina cœlesti, eius rei argumentum est: sed etiam grauissimi Apostoli Pauli iudicium, quod secutus, in ardua illa de Iustificatione fidei disputatione, nobile dictum: Iustus aut ex fide sua vivet (Rom.i. 17.) ex hoc Propheta depromsit: nequaquam id facturus, si de Prophetiæ istius auctoritate pij homines dubitauissent.
main_text.head: I. NOMEN.

page.notes: Greek word after "docendi gratia" is not fully legible on the scan; the first letters are uncertain and the rest could not be read reliably, so it is marked [?] and partly unread. The Greek word before "Habacuci" is read as συμφωνία and is fairly clear. The Greek word "ὑπόληψιν" is a best reading with [?]. The Latin "Gaussæ" is read from the scan with some doubt. The Latin "(Rom.i." is printed with a small i in place of a numeral and is copied as printed. The catchword "gen-" is at lower right.
